issues.legal_issue: Rent-control remedies for fixing standard rent and restoring essential services remain available to tenants of public premises when those matters are not governed by the special public-premises law.
material_facts: The tenant occupied premises owned by a statutory public corporation under a continuing tenancy.
The landlord disputed the rent payable, and the tenant applied for fixation of standard rent under the applicable rent-control law.
The tenant and other occupants had also sought restoration of lift service under that law after the lift failed to work properly.
No eviction proceeding had been brought against the tenant.
The special public-premises law provided for eviction of unauthorized occupants and recovery of rent or damages, but did not provide for standard-rent fixation or restoration of essential services.
The rent-control law did not exempt these public premises from its application and had received presidential assent.
issues.conclusion: The rent-control law’s provisions for fixing standard rent and restoring essential services are not repugnant to the special public-premises law, and applications for those remedies are maintainable under the rent-control law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 254(2) of the Constitution, repugnancy requires the enactments to cover the same field in a manner that creates a real conflict; provisions addressing distinct matters may operate together. The rent-control law provides for standard-rent fixation and restoration of essential services, while the special public-premises law addresses eviction of unauthorized occupants and recovery of rent or damages. The Court applied the principles in Hoechst Pharmaceuticals Ltd. v. State of Bihar, State of West Bengal v. Kesoram Industries Ltd., M. Karunanidhi v. Union of India, and Vijay Kumar Sharma v. State of Karnataka. It distinguished Ashoka Marketing Ltd. v. Punjab National Bank, which concerned eviction, and approved the approach in Bharath Gold Mines Ltd. v. Kannappa.

rule.if: tenant_remedy_proceeding and premises_owned_by_public_body and remedy_concerns_rent_fixation_or_essential_service and subject_not_governed_by_special_public_premises_law and rent_control_law_covers_subject

predicates.tenant_remedy_proceeding: A tenant of premises owned by a public body brought a proceeding to obtain a remedy concerning the tenancy.
predicates.premises_owned_by_public_body: A public body owned the premises occupied by the tenant.
predicates.remedy_concerns_rent_fixation_or_essenti: The tenant sought fixation of rent or restoration of an essential service.
predicates.subject_not_governed_by_special_public_p: The special law governing public premises did not provide for the subject of the tenant’s requested remedy.
predicates.rent_control_law_covers_subject: The applicable rent-control law provided for the subject of the tenant’s requested remedy.

issues.definition: When a tenant of publicly owned premises seeks a remedy covered by rent-control law but not by the special law governing public premises, the rent-control remedy remains available.

issues.legal_issue: The special public-premises law governs proceedings to evict unauthorized occupants and recover rent or damages for unauthorized occupation of public premises.
material_facts: The occupied premises belonged to a statutory public corporation and were public premises under the applicable law.
The parties accepted that the public-premises law applied to the premises for eviction and recovery of arrears of rent.
The special public-premises law provided procedures for eviction of unauthorized occupants and recovery of rent or damages, and barred court proceedings concerning those matters.
issues.conclusion: The special public-premises law governs eviction of unauthorized occupants and recovery of rent or damages for unauthorized occupation; the rent-control law does not provide an alternative forum for those matters.
issues.legal_principle: The Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971 provides a special procedure for eviction and recovery of rent or damages, with jurisdiction barred for the matters specified in section 15. The Court relied on Ashoka Marketing Ltd. v. Punjab National Bank and the decisions in Kaiser-I-Hind Pvt. Ltd. v. National Textile Corporation (Maharashtra North) Ltd. and Crawford Bayley & Co. v. Union of India, while distinguishing remedies concerning matters the special law does not cover.

rule.if: public_premises_enforcement_proceeding and premises_owned_by_public_body and claim_seeks_eviction_or_recovery_for_unauthorized_occupation and special_law_provides_procedure_for_claim

predicates.public_premises_enforcement_proceeding: A public body brought a proceeding concerning its premises against an occupant.
predicates.premises_owned_by_public_body: A public body owned the premises occupied by the person against whom the proceeding was brought.
predicates.claim_seeks_eviction_or_recovery_for_una: The proceeding sought eviction of an unauthorized occupant or recovery of rent or damages for unauthorized occupation.
predicates.special_law_provides_procedure_for_claim: A special law provided a procedure for resolving the claim.

issues.definition: When a public body brings a covered proceeding concerning unauthorized occupation of its premises, the procedure provided by the special law governs that claim.
